title: S3.7c local elliptic ACIS cone projection and distance

scope.geometry: Closest point and unsigned Euclidean distance to the untrimmed elliptic-cone surface under the explicit local decoded-field parameterization
scope.domain: Finite cone face with a positive finite ratio other than one, positive cosine angle, normalized angle pair within caller frame tolerance, nonzero axis and projected major axis, finite query, and numerically resolvable normalized generator direction; zero sine angle dispatches to the elliptic-cylinder limit
scope.algorithm: For nonzero sine angle, represent each surface generator as a line through the local cone apex; maximize the squared query-direction dot product over direction norm. A half-angle substitution gives a quartic stationarity polynomial; recursive derivative-root isolation and bisection find roots on two bounded charts, and endpoints are included as candidates. At zero sine angle, reuse the ellipse closest-point solver in the axis-normal plane.
scope.ambiguity_policy: Projection refuses tied distinct closest points, including symmetric axial cases. Distance-only queries accept non-unique minima. The exact apex has one geometric closest point.
unsupported_profiles: ratios or angles whose normalized direction component squares underflow
scope.tolerance_policy: Projection uses the caller frame tolerance; distance checks an explicit finite nonnegative linear tolerance with equality accepted
scope.numeric_policy: Scale world/query/reference geometry before solving; isolate polynomial roots in [-1,1] charts; reject non-finite or unresolvable candidates; construct output coordinates using exponent-scaled products and compensated sums
non_claims: normative ACIS ratio, nappe, orientation, or parameter semantics
edge trims, pcurves, or finite face-domain clipping
B-rep validity, manifoldness, or shell closure
native consumer or independent-kernel semantic qualification

validation.symbol_check: PASS (nm -gC build-gcc/libdxfrw.a exports the cone evaluator, projection, and distance symbols)
